heading_path.text: Appendix G. The TEC-1G as TEC-OS uses it

inventory_evidence.full_context:
The CPU generates the serial bits itself. It sends through `01h` bit 6 and
receives through `03h` bit 7. The connection uses 4800 baud, eight data bits,
no parity and two stop bits. The delay counts assume a 4 MHz clock, so the
board requires FAST with the 4 MHz oscillator (`tools/build.mjs:25-26`,
`tools/build.mjs:37-76`, `src/console.asm:387-421`,
`src/console.asm:452-492`).

heading_path.text: Appendix G. The TEC-1G as TEC-OS uses it
The hex keypad and its NMI

inventory_evidence.full_context:
With the keypad NMI jumper fitted, a press raises a non-maskable interrupt. The
CPU pushes its return address and enters `0066h`, inside the default file
control block (FCB) at `005Ch–007Fh`. TEC-OS installs no NMI handler there. The
bytes can be file metadata rather than instructions, so a press can crash the
machine. The supported TEC-OS setup leaves the jumper off. The diagnostics ROM
has its own NMI test and different keypad instructions, which must not be
applied to an ordinary TEC-OS session.

heading_path.text: Appendix H. The service file format

inventory_evidence.full_context:
A service file contains the bytes to install, the records it needs and the
positions that require relocation. Its on-disk header describes that work.
The loader overwrites some fields after using them, so an installed header
must be read differently from the file header below.
[Write a resident service](13-write-a-resident-service.md) covers authoring.
[Loading and removing services](24-loading-and-removing-services.md) follows
installation and gives the resident header. This reference retains a
historical GLCD.SVC dump to show the file fields and gap encoding together.

inventory_evidence.full_context:
`?` matches one character, including a padding space. `*` fills the rest of
its field with question marks. Thus `G*.*` is `G???????.???`. Text after a
star in the same field is ignored, so `D*X` and `D*` select the same pattern.
A short field is padded with spaces. `????.COM` therefore matches names of
up to four characters with type COM, not every name ending in COM
(`src/cpm/ccpcmd.asm:617-645`, `src/cpm/ccpcmd.asm:706-727`).

nearest_heading.text: A COM program and its calls

heading_path.text: A COM program and its calls

inventory_evidence.full_context:
Registers hold the values passed to a call. `A`, `B`, `C` and `E` each
hold a byte. `BC`, `DE` and `HL` are 16-bit register pairs, large enough
for a memory address. To select a BDOS operation, you put its function number in `C` and
call `0005h`. A byte parameter goes in `E`, while an address or word
parameter goes in `DE`. A byte result is returned in `A` and a word result
in `HL`. For example, function 2 takes the character in `E` and function 9
takes an address in `DE`. In source, `BDOS EQU $0005` gives that call
address a name.
